certificate_verdict.note: the MSE-proxy certificate does not predict the measured accuracy crossing. The spectrum-level finding that does survive: the frozen sparse code's linear span captures ~3.4x more one-hot label power than the dense trunk's (11.8% vs 3.5%), which is why the sparse family has more room to keep improving with data. But its captured modes decay faster (effective rank 8 vs 30), so they are learned slower; and the measured ACCURACY crossing is an argmax phenomenon over 345 one-hot channels that the scalar MSE proxy does not track. A classification-aware certificate (per-class score-margin prediction) is the registered follow-up if this direction is re-opened.
certificate_verdict.registered_conclusion_licenses: M121 fires under the registered gate; the firing is about the MSE proxy, not about the existence of learnable label power in the sparse span.

gate.gap_direction_at_nmax: predicted E_g^sparse(n_max) < E_g^dense(n_max) (matches M116's measured sparse accuracy 0.2153 > dense 0.1972)
gate.predicted_crossing: smallest ladder P where predicted E_g^sparse(P) <= E_g^dense(P); PASS if it lies within a factor [1/3, 3] of the measured crossing interval midpoint (M116: sparse overtakes between n=27600 and n=55200, midpoint 41400)

source.features: reuses M116's sealed feature memmaps (data_cache_root()/v16/m116/f_train.npy 138000x12288 float32; dense_train.npy 138000x768 float32); no re-encoding, no training
source.m116_reference: logs/results/v16/m116_scale/evidence.json (measured Q(n); sparse overtakes dense between n=27600 and n=55200)

theory.disclosure: E_g is an MSE proxy for one-hot classification; the gate is the predicted CROSSING (shape-level), not absolute error values. Target power in kernel-null modes is a constant shift to both curves and is reported, not gated.
theory.eigenvalues: eta_rho = eigenvalues of (1/M) F_std^T F_std, the discrete-measure kernel PCA of the linear kernel on the STANDARDISED frozen features (M = 138000 train rows, the measure the head was fit on; per-dim mean/unit-variance from train, the M116 RidgeAccumulator convention)
theory.formula: Canatar-Bordelon-Pehlevan 2006.13198 eq.(4), noise-free: E_g(P) = (1/(1-gamma)) * sum_rho [ eta_rho * kappa^2 / (kappa + P*eta_rho)^2 ] * w2_rho, with kappa = lambda + sum_rho kappa*eta_rho/(kappa + P*eta_rho), gamma = sum_rho P*eta_rho^2/(kappa + P*eta_rho)^2
theory.modal_power: w2_rho = sum over classes c of a_rho,c^2 / (M*eta_rho), a_rho,c = v_rho^T (F_std^T y_c) = projection of the one-hot label vector of class c onto feature eigenvector rho
theory.ridge_mapping: the program's RidgeAccumulator standardises then adds the penalty to the Gram diagonal, i.e. minimises ||F_std w - y||^2 + penalty*||w||^2 = Canatar's objective with lambda = penalty = 1.0

config.title: Spectral learning-curve certificate: does the Canatar-Bordelon-Pehlevan theory (2006.13198 / 2002.02561) predict M116's measured Q(n) crossing from the feature Gram eigenspectra alone, without retraining?

kill_switch_1_crossing.registered: predicted crossing within factor [1/3, 3] of the measured M116 crossing midpoint (41400); the crossing is read off the LEARNABLE-part curves (null-mode power is reported, not gated, per the registered disclosure)

kill_switch_2_gap_direction.registered: predicted sparse error < dense error at n_max (matches measured accuracy order)

lambda_grid_sensitivity.note: robustness of the predicted crossing to the ridge constant (the mapping to the program's penalty is exact at lambda=1.0)

measure.standardise: per-dim mean/unit-variance over the rows used

question: does the Canatar-Bordelon-Pehlevan learning-curve theory, from the feature Gram spectra alone, predict M116's measured Q(n) crossing?

dense._tail_note: tail_index = slope of log(eta) vs log(rank) over the top half (more negative = faster-decaying spectrum = stronger spectral bias = steeper learning curve at fixed n)
